title: API aggregators: types, examples and how AI agents use them
summary: An API aggregator puts many APIs behind one interface. Compare unified and data API aggregators, and see how Firecrawl Alexandria serves AI agents.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR**


- **Firecrawl Alexandria is an API aggregator for the data AI agents need.** One Firecrawl account or API key reaches data providers such as SEC EDGAR, Fiscal.ai, Apollo and Best Buy, plus Firecrawl's Government & Legal, Research and Developer indexes. Finding tools is free, and every tool lists its price in Firecrawl credits.
- **An API aggregator puts many third-party APIs behind one interface** , so you sign up, authenticate and pay once instead of once per provider.
- **Firecrawl works in ChatGPT, Claude and any MCP client.** Developers get the same tools through the REST API, SDKs and CLI.


---


Firecrawl Alexandria lets an AI agent describe the data it needs, find the provider that holds it and call that provider with the Firecrawl key it already has. Standing in for many integrations with one is the job of an API aggregator. The term covers products that solve different problems, so this guide explains how they work, how they differ and where Firecrawl fits.


## What is an API aggregator?


API aggregators sit between your code and many third-party APIs and expose them through one interface. You create one account, use one credential and learn one request format, while the aggregator deals with each provider's own keys, schemas, errors and billing behind the scenes.


API aggregation changes five things compared with calling each provider yourself:


Calling each API directly Calling through an API aggregator


Accounts and keys One per provider One


Authentication Each provider's own flow: API keys, OAuth or signed requests One flow


Request and response formats Learned and mapped per provider One documented format or a shared data model


Billing A plan or contract per provider One bill


Adding a source A new integration project A new call


An aggregator covers the providers and fields it supports. A provider outside its catalog still needs a direct integration, which is why the size and shape of the catalog matters as much as the interface.


## How is a data API aggregator different from a unified API?


A data API aggregator such as Firecrawl Alexandria returns data that providers own, such as SEC filings, company profiles or retail prices, and you call it with your own key. A unified API returns data your customer owns, from their own SaaS accounts, after that customer signs in. One answers lookups about the world, and the other syncs a customer's records.


Data API aggregator (Firecrawl Alexandria) Unified API


Whose data Providers': public records, licensed publishers and Firecrawl's own indexes Your customers': records in their own apps


Who signs in You, once, with a Firecrawl account or API key Each customer, through OAuth


Typical calls Search, look up and retrieve Read and sync records, with writes on some vendors


Data shape Each tool documents its own inputs and response A shared model per category


Pricing Each tool lists its price per call in Firecrawl credits Set by each vendor


Typical caller AI agents and apps that need facts SaaS products that need their customers' data


The two often sit in the same product. A sales tool can sync a customer's CRM accounts through a unified API while its agent enriches the same accounts with funding, headcount and filings through Firecrawl Alexandria.


### How does a unified API work for SaaS integrations?


A unified API maps every app in one software category, such as CRM or HR, to a shared data model. Your customer connects their own account through a sign-in component the unified API vendor provides, the vendor stores the credentials, and your product reads or writes records like contacts, invoices or employees through one set of endpoints.


Unified APIs exist because SaaS stacks keep growing. BetterCloud's[2026 State of SaaS report](https://www.bettercloud.com/monitor/the-2026-state-of-saas-report/) , a survey of 525 IT and security professionals published in July 2026, found the average number of apps per organization up **11%** year over year, with AI tools driving the growth. Every new app a customer adopts is another integration request for the products they use.


That request lands on the roadmap fast. One[DEV Community post](https://dev.to/kasfen/best-enterprise-ai-integration-infrastructure-platforms-and-frameworks-for-ai-product-integration-l7k) from June 2026 describes an enterprise buyer asking whether an AI product can read SharePoint and write to Salesforce, at which point "half the roadmap turns into connector engineering."


For a B2B product, each app a unified API adds is one more integration request it can say yes to. That is why vendors pitch them on winning deals, keeping customers and entering regions where customers run different apps.


Unified API vendors differ on three points. Check how many of the fields you need sit in the shared model, whether the vendor copies customer data into its own store or passes each request through to the source app, and whether you can write records back.


## Why do AI agents need an API aggregator?


AI agents decide which data they need while a task runs, so integrations a developer wired up in advance only go so far. Our guide to[how AI agents use APIs](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/api-for-ai-agents) covers the integration patterns behind that. An API aggregator gives an agent one credential, a way to search for the right tool, and each tool's inputs and price before it spends anything.


Agents already depend on APIs. Postman's[2026 State of the API report](https://blog.postman.com/the-2026-state-of-the-api-report-agents-are-in-production-and-most-apis-arent-ready/) , a survey of 8,953 developers, architects and executives published in November 2026, found that **one in four** organizations run AI agents that call APIs in production. Only **13.2%** say their APIs are fully ready for agents, and **37.7%** haven't enabled any way for agents to discover their APIs.


Companies want agents to make those calls without a person in the loop. In Box's[2026 State of AI in the Enterprise](https://blog.box.com/SAI26-agentic-ai-is-here) survey of 1,640 IT decision-makers, run by The Harris Poll and published in June 2026, **79%** said it's important or critical that agents connect directly to systems, APIs and data sources without a human interface.


The data those agents need is often the hardest to reach. Firecrawl's November 2026 white paper,[AI's Search-Bar Problem](https://www.firecrawl.dev/whitepapers/ais-search-bar-problem) , puts it this way:


> Much of what matters most sits a little out of reach. Registries live behind search forms. Filings live in databases. Research papers live behind indexes.


Developers building agents describe the same problem. In a[September 2026 post on X](https://x.com/PrachitiParkar/status/2102257204892246195) , Prachiti Parkar summed up a personal agent that works across travel, email, calendars and payments as "One agent. So many tools. So many integrations." She points out that an agent starts with a goal and has to discover and choose its tools at runtime.[Uber Engineering](https://x.com/UberEng/status/2106071967619322330) wrote in October 2026 that before it built a central MCP gateway, teams built integrations independently and tools were "hard to discover."


Even small workflows stitch several sources together. Andrew Allsop built one that joins Firecrawl and the Companies House API to qualify new signups for a friend's business:


Companies House is one of the public registries an agent can call through Firecrawl Alexandria, with the same key it uses for Firecrawl /search and /scrape.


### Why use a third-party API aggregation platform?


A third-party platform takes over the work that grows with every provider you add. These benefits matter most for agents:


- **Less integration work.** Engineers build to one API instead of one per provider, and keeping each provider connection working when its API changes becomes the platform's job, not yours.
- **New sources without new code.** When a provider joins Firecrawl Alexandria, agents find its tools through the same search they already run, so coverage grows without a release.
- **Automatic fallback routing.** When one provider has no answer, the platform tries the next one. Firecrawl's people and company enrichment tries providers in order of listed price and past success rate, stops at the first one that finds each field, and charges nothing for a miss.
- **Consolidated billing.** You pay one bill instead of holding a contract and invoice with every provider. Every Firecrawl Alexandria tool bills in Firecrawl credits on your Firecrawl plan.
- **Fewer rate limits to juggle.** You manage one account's limits instead of a separate quota with each provider. Firecrawl lists its limits per plan in its[rate limits docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/rate-limits) .
- **Broad compatibility.** The platform should work wherever your agent runs. Firecrawl Alexandria works from ChatGPT, Claude and any MCP client, plus the REST API, SDKs and CLI, as the setup steps below show.


## How does Firecrawl Alexandria work as an API aggregator?


Firecrawl Alexandria is a library of data providers that AI agents reach through one Firecrawl API key, MCP server or CLI. It works like an aggregator: instead of signing up for each data API separately, you search the whole catalog and call any provider through the same connection.


An agent describes what it needs, gets matching tools from many providers at no cost, reads each tool's inputs and price in Firecrawl credits, then runs the tool with the same Firecrawl account or API key. Providers range from public registries and licensed publishers to Firecrawl's own indexes.


Each call follows three steps:


1. **Find.** Firecrawl /search with` sources: \["alexandria"\]` returns ranked tools for free. Add` "web"` to the sources to get web results in the same call, billed as a normal search.
2. **Check.** Find Tools returns a tool's inputs, response format and price in Firecrawl credits before anything runs, and it's free too. Agents on the Firecrawl MCP server read the same contracts through its Alexandria library tools.
3. **Run.** Firecrawl /scrape with an` alexandria` block (provider, capability and options) runs the tool and bills its listed price.


One search can surface tools from several providers. A request for a public company's annual report filings, for example, can return tools from both SEC EDGAR and Fiscal.ai, and the agent picks by inputs and price. For people and company data, the Firecrawl MCP server runs the fallback waterfall described above, and our[Firecrawl MCP v3 post](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/firecrawl-mcp-v3) covers it in detail.


[Credal](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/credal-firecrawl-ai-agents) , which runs AI agents for enterprise customers, describes the problem an aggregator removes:


> Our customers need their agents to reference today's facts or pull from their customer-facing support docs without building a custom integration.


*[Jack Fischer](https://www.linkedin.com/in/jackfischer11/) , Co-Founder and CTO,[Credal](https://www.credal.ai/)*


### What makes Firecrawl Alexandria a strong API aggregator for agents?


Six things make Firecrawl Alexandria a good fit for agents that call APIs on their own:


- **Broad coverage.** Providers cover finance, company and people data, public records, retail, health, travel, sports and more, next to Firecrawl's own Government & Legal, Research and Developer indexes. The table below links every category.
- **Accurate, structured data.** Each tool returns typed records with a named source instead of a scraped page the agent has to clean up. In tests reported in the[Firecrawl Alexandria launch post](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/introducing-alexandria-series-b) , agents using Firecrawl Alexandria scored **21% higher on answer quality** than agents using built-in web tools, across 845 tasks with the same model and prompts and blind AI judging.
- **Clear commercial licensing.** Firecrawl pays official data providers under agreement, and a provider with its own terms shows them to an admin on your Firecrawl team before the first call.
- **Fallback built in.** People and company lookups through the Firecrawl MCP server try several providers in one call and move to the next when one comes back empty, so a single provider's gap doesn't stop the agent. For other data, one search often returns tools from more than one provider, which gives the agent a second source to try.
- **Pricing that scales.** Each tool has one listed price in Firecrawl credits, and the same credits run from the free plan up to Scale and Enterprise plans, so you don't switch products as volume grows.
- **Proven in production.** The public[rankings page](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/rankings) showed 5.3 million agent calls through Firecrawl Alexandria in the 24 hours before this post.


Users rate it well too. On G2, Firecrawl Alexandria holds a[4.5 out of 5 rating from 300+ reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/firecrawl-alexandria/reviews) and Firecrawl holds[4.7 out of 5 from 1,500+ reviews](https://www.g2.com/products/firecrawl/reviews) , as of November 2026. One verified reviewer at a small business wrote that Firecrawl Alexandria "solves the headache of building and maintaining dozens of separate API integrations, authentication keys, and billing accounts for our AI agents."

## How do you connect Firecrawl Alexandria to ChatGPT, Claude or your own agent?


Firecrawl Alexandria also takes the technical work out of getting data to agents, for developers and non-developers alike. As more teams put AI agents to work, those agents are only as good as the data they can reach, and with Firecrawl Alexandria that data arrives through one MCP connection. In ChatGPT, it's as simple as installing the Firecrawl plugin and signing in. There are no servers to set up, no provider keys to manage and no integrations to maintain.


Firecrawl connects to ChatGPT through a plugin, to Claude through a connector, and to any other AI agent through the Firecrawl MCP server. Each one signs in to your Firecrawl account, so there is no API key to paste, and the whole Firecrawl Alexandria catalog is available as soon as you connect.


- **ChatGPT:** open **Plugins** , search for **Firecrawl** , select **Install** and sign in.
- **Claude:** add the Firecrawl connector from the connector directory, sign in, then turn it on from the **+** menu.
- **Claude Code:** run` claude mcp add --transport http firecrawl https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` , then finish signing in from` /mcp` .
- **Codex:** install the Firecrawl plugin in the Codex app, or run` codex mcp add firecrawl --url https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` and then` codex mcp login firecrawl` .
- **Cursor or any MCP client with a JSON config:** add` https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth` as a server named` firecrawl` .


[Add Firecrawl to ChatGPT](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a314a73f8ac819195b0d55e36b9c609?q=firecrawl)


[Add Firecrawl to Claude](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/firecrawl)

### How do developers call Firecrawl Alexandria?


Developers can call every Firecrawl Alexandria tool from the[Python, Node.js, Go and Rust SDKs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/overview) , the[REST API](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/features/alexandria) or the[Firecrawl CLI](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/sdks/cli) . This Python example finds filing tools across providers for free, reads one tool's inputs and price, then calls SEC EDGAR with the same key:


```text
import   os
from   firecrawl   import   Firecrawl


firecrawl   =   Firecrawl  (api_key  =  os.environ[  "FIRECRAWL_API_KEY"  ])


# 1. Describe the data you need. Tool discovery is free.
found   =   firecrawl  .  search  (
"latest annual report filings for a public company"  ,
sources  =  [  "alexandria"  ],
limit  =  5  ,
)
for   tool   in   found  .  tools   or   []  :
print  (  f  "  {  tool.provider  }  /  {  tool.capability  }  "  )


# 2. Read the chosen tool's inputs and price before running it. Also free.
contract   =   firecrawl  .  find_tools  (
providers  =  [  "sec-gov"  ],
capabilities  =  [  "filings/filings"  ],
level  =  "tools"  ,
expand  =  [  "options"  ],
).  items  [  0  ]
print  (contract[  "id"  ], contract[  "creditsCost"  ],   "credits per call"  )
print  ([option[  "name"  ]   for   option   in   contract[  "options"  ]])


# 3. Run it with the same Firecrawl API key.
filings   =   firecrawl  .  scrape  (
alexandria  =  {
**  contract[  "execute"  ],
"options"  : {  "ticker"  :   "NVDA"  ,   "forms"  : [  "10-K"  ],   "limit"  :   3  },
},
)
for   filing   in   filings  .  alexandria  [  0  ].  data  [  "filings"  ]:
print  (filing[  "form"  ], filing[  "filing_date"  ], filing[  "primary_document_url"  ])
```


The search returns tools from more than one provider, Find Tools returns the chosen tool's price and inputs, and the scrape returns the filings as structured records:

fiscal-ai/filings/list
sec-gov/filings/companies_get
sec-gov/filings/sections
sec-gov/filings/filing

sec-gov/filings/daily_index_list

## How do you choose the right API aggregator?


The right API aggregator depends on whose data you need and who calls it. Firecrawl Alexandria fits AI agents and apps that need facts from providers on demand, such as filings, company records, prices, research or public records. A unified API fits products that read and write their customers' CRM, HR or accounting records.


Many products use more than one. Our guide to[APIs for AI agents](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/api-for-ai-agents) covers how unified APIs, MCP servers and direct calls fit together in one agent, and our[guide to RapidAPI alternatives](https://www.firecrawl.dev/blog/rapidapi-alternatives) compares the data API marketplaces.


### What should you check before you pick an API aggregator?


An aggregator sits in the path of every call, so its speed, uptime, pricing and data handling become yours. These are the checks that matter most:


Check What to look for How Firecrawl Alexandria handles it


Latency Whether calls reach the provider live or come from a cache, and how long a typical call takes, since an agent waits on each call mid-task[Benchmarks](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/benchmarks) compare tools on quality, speed and cost, and[rankings](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/rankings) show what agents call most


Reliability and uptime A public status page, and a cheap way to test tools before you build on them[Firecrawl status](https://status.firecrawl.dev/) shows live status and 90-day uptime history, and inspecting a tool is free


Pricing transparency A price per call you can see before the call runs, and clear rules for calls that find nothing Each tool lists its price in Firecrawl credits before it runs, and in the people and company waterfall a miss is free


Data privacy A current security audit, clear retention terms and a DPA Firecrawl is SOC 2 Type II, and[Enterprise](https://www.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) plans add zero data retention and a DPA


Data sources Where each record comes from and whether the platform has an agreement with the source Each tool names its source, and Firecrawl pays official data providers under agreement


The red flags are the reverse of that table. Watch for prices you only see on the invoice, no public status page, records with no named source, and no way to inspect a tool before you pay for it.


## How much does Firecrawl Alexandria cost?


Finding a Firecrawl Alexandria tool is free, and each tool shows its price in Firecrawl credits before it runs. Searches of the Government & Legal Index and the Research Index cost nothing, and Scale and Enterprise plans have no daily limit on them. The Firecrawl free plan includes 1,000 Firecrawl credits a month, and paid plans start at $19 a month billed monthly, or $16 a month billed annually, for 5,000 Firecrawl credits.


Christopher Porter uses Firecrawl for professional research and called it "well worth a subscription."


Firecrawl Alexandria needs a signed-in Firecrawl account or a Firecrawl API key. Some providers, such as Apollo and FullEnrich, ask an admin on your Firecrawl team to accept their terms once before the first call. Each provider page on[Firecrawl Alexandria](https://alexandria.firecrawl.dev/providers) lists its tools and prices, and[pricing](https://www.firecrawl.dev/pricing) has the plan details.


Teams that need a security review can start with the[enterprise page](https://www.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) and the[security docs](https://docs.firecrawl.dev/enterprise) .
